_comment: Policy that is stated in more than one skill, and the exact sentences that must
A skill loads its own SKILL.md and nothing else, so shared policy has to be
repeated rather than extracted — a rule living in a file the model may not read
is not a rule. The repetition is deliberate. The drift is what this file stops.
`invariants` are matched with whitespace collapsed, so rewrapping a paragraph is
not drift. Rewording one sentence in one skill is.
See evals/README.md for how to add a block.

blocks.policy: How a skill accumulates the user's corrections in corpus/LESSONS.md
blocks.why: Three skills write to one file in the user's private repo. If they disagree about where lessons live, how a wrong one is retired, or whether a skill may edit itself, the kit starts rewriting its own prompts in someone's corpus. The retirement markup has to be one form: every session parses it, and a form only one skill knows is a live rule everywhere else.
invariants: This skill ships generic. It gets sharper by accumulating the user's own corrections in `corpus/LESSONS.md` — in their **private** corpus repo, never in the kit.
**At the start of a session, read `corpus/LESSONS.md`** if it exists. Treat each entry as an additional rule for this user, on equal footing with the hard rules above.
append one dated line to `corpus/LESSONS.md`: the mistake, and the rule to apply next time. One line each. Nothing already in the file is deleted.
**Route it before you write it: would this rule still hold if the corpus were about someone else?**
a rule nobody can diff is a rule nobody can review, port, or undo

**When a lesson proves wrong, retire it rather than appending its opposite.** Two entries that contradict each other both arrive with equal footing in every later session. Retire in the session where the lesson misfired and only on the user's explicit say-so, by marking the entry in place: `~~<the entry>~~ retired YYYY-MM-DD: <one clause of why>`. A struck entry is history and is never applied again.
**Never edit this SKILL.md to record a lesson,** and never write lessons into the kit repo.

exempt.bootstrap: Creates LESSONS.md and explains it once, retirement included; runs before there is anything to correct.
exempt.compact: Explicitly forbidden from touching LESSONS.md — pruning the scar tissue defeats it, and a wrong entry is retired where it misfired.
exempt.prep: Sends the session to read render's SKILL.md for the rulebook and writes no lessons of its own; the four rules it restates are in prep-render-invariants.

blocks.policy: _inbox/ is a queue of raw material, never a source
blocks.why: The single rule the whole trust model rests on. It is stated in the skill that fills the inbox, the skill that renders past it, and the skill that opens an application with a recruiter writing into it. All three have to mean the same thing by it.
invariants: Folder location is a truth claim
never rendered from and never cited as fact

exempt.bootstrap: Points at the interview skill's rules rather than restating them.
exempt.compact: Never reads _inbox/; it prunes vetted story files.
exempt.prep: States the sharper application-specific version — a recruiter is selling a job.
exempt.render: States it as the sourcing rule (see candidate-claim-sourcing), not the storage rule.

blocks.policy: Private individuals' names stay out of filenames and folder names
blocks.why: Both skills that name files after a human interaction repeat this, for the same reason: a filename is visible in a screen-share to someone who may work at that company.
invariants: Roles in filenames, names in the body if the user wants them. Filenames get screenshotted, screen-shared and tab-completed in front of other people

exempt.bootstrap: Creates no file named after a person.
exempt.interview: Carries the broader no-names-anywhere rule for story bodies.
exempt.render: Carries the broader no-names-anywhere rule for artifact prose.

blocks.policy: A claim about the candidate comes from the vetted corpus and nowhere else
blocks.why: This is the rule that broke. apply and render each stated it, differently enough that render's version contradicted render's own workflow — it barred reading the folder it was told to read. The distinction that keeps it coherent is candidate claims vs employer context, and both skills must draw it the same way.
invariants: Never source a claim about the candidate from `applications/`

exempt.interview: Writes to the corpus rather than reading from applications/.
exempt.prep: Carries the positive form of the rule under prep-render-invariants, not this folder-scoped bar.
exempt.render: States the same rule as the three source domains — see the superseded list below for the wording it may not go back to.

blocks.policy: The four render rules prep restates rather than leaving to its read of render's SKILL.md
blocks.why: render's whole rulebook governs a prep pack, and sibling skill loading is not guaranteed — a skill loads its own SKILL.md and nothing else — so prep carries that inheritance as an explicit step: read render's SKILL.md before writing any pack file. These four are copied on top of the step because they are the ones a prep pack fails on. A copy still binds if the read gets skipped, and it is what makes them checkable here.
invariants: Every claim about the candidate comes from the vetted corpus, and from nothing else.
Numbers carry their source and their ceiling.
No names of non-public people. No internal codenames.

exempt.apply: Opens the folder and runs the fit check; the artifacts themselves are render's and prep's.
exempt.compact: Renders nothing — it prunes the corpus these rules read from.
exempt.interview: Writes the vetted claims these rules spend, and states its own capture-side versions.

superseded.why: Read as a bar on ever marking an entry, which left a lesson that proved wrong with no exit but a contradicting entry beside it — two rules of equal footing in every later session. The file still only grows; a wrong entry is struck in place instead.

superseded.text: Nothing in `applications/` is ever a source for a render
superseded.why: Absolute and wrong. render must read jd.md and fit.md — that handoff is most of what apply exists to produce. The bar is on claims about the candidate, not on reading the folder.

Describes application.md as storing a stage and a next action, both of which rule 6 forbids: the stage is the last line of the log, and a stored next action is a to-do on its own schedule. This description drifted into three files — apply's own folder tree, render/REFERENCE.md's table, and the README — so the skill contradicted its own rule in the places a reader looks first.

superseded.text: Never render from `_inbox/`, and never from `applications/`
superseded.why: Same absolute reading, in render's own rule 1. It contradicted workflow step 2 four screens below it.
